fields.System.Title: OUT-6 — Shipping
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Load cartons onto a vehicle, confirm dispatch, and tell everyone who needs to know that the
goods have gone.

Scope

In. Shipment creation, carton scanning, dispatch confirmation, manifests, ERP notification,
partial shipment.

Out. Carrier booking and rate shopping. Tracking-number allocation by the carrier's own
system.

Design notes

Dispatch is the point of no return. After it, only a return brings stock back. That makes
OUT-603 a story that deserves a rollback test and an idempotency test, not just a happy-path
one.

Confirming dispatch does four things in one transaction: moves stock to VIRT-CUSTOMER,
writes movements, releases any leftover reservations for those orders, and sets order status to
shipped. Missing the reservation release leaves stock permanently reserved against a shipped
order.

Confirm only after the physical load is complete. Confirming while loading is still in
progress produces records saying "shipped" for goods still on the dock — and if the vehicle
leaves without them, nobody finds out until the customer calls.

A carton ships exactly once. Unique constraint on carton-to-shipment. A carton scanned onto
two shipments makes both manifests wrong.

The ERP notification goes through the outbox, never as a direct call inside the
transaction. A slow ERP must not slow dispatch, and a failed call must not lose the invoice
trigger.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Carton loaded onto the wrong vehicle | [doc 05 WF 8](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Dispatch confirmed before loading finishes | [doc 05 WF 8](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Reservations not released on ship | [doc 09 §5.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Same shipment confirmed twice | [doc 09 §3.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| ERP notification lost | [doc 09 §2.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
